what_its_for: Ranolazine is used to treat chronic stable angina, which is chest pain or pressure that happens when your heart is not getting enough oxygen. It helps reduce how often you have chest pain episodes so you can be more active in your daily life. It is usually used when other angina medicines have not worked well enough on their own.
how_to_take: Swallow the tablet whole with or without food. Do NOT crush, chew, or break the tablet, as this can release too much medicine at once and cause serious side effects. Try to take it at the same times each day to keep a steady level of medicine in your body.
dosing: The usual starting dose is 500 mg twice a day (once in the morning and once in the evening, about 12 hours apart). Your doctor may increase your dose to 1,000 mg twice a day if needed and if you tolerate it well. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions for your dose.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do NOT take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store ranolazine at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Store it in a dry place such as a dresser drawer or cabinet, not in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets.
what_to_avoid: Avoid eating large amounts of grapefruit or drinking grapefruit juice, as it can increase the level of ranolazine in your blood and raise the risk of side effects. Do not take ranolazine with certain medicines without talking to your doctor first, including some antibiotics (like clarithromycin), antifungals (like ketoconazole), HIV medicines, or other heart medicines. Avoid drinking excessive amounts of alcohol. Tell your doctor and pharmacist about ALL medicines, vitamins, and supplements you take before starting ranolazine.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek emergency help if you experience: a fast, slow, or irregular heartbeat or pounding in your chest; severe dizziness or fainting; feeling like you might pass out; numbness or tingling in your hands or feet; severe nausea or vomiting; signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, itching, swelling of the face, lips, or throat, or difficulty breathing. Also let your doctor know if your chest pain does not improve or gets worse, or if you have any new or unusual symptoms.
when_it_works: Ranolazine does not work right away like a nitroglycerin tablet to stop a sudden chest pain attack. It works over time to reduce how often chest pain happens. You may start to notice fewer angina episodes within the first few weeks of taking it regularly. Keep taking it every day as prescribed, even if you feel well.
special_populations: Older adults (age 65 and over): You may be more sensitive to side effects such as dizziness. Use caution when standing up quickly to avoid falls. Kidney problems: Tell your doctor if you have kidney disease, as dose adjustments may be needed. Liver problems: Ranolazine should NOT be used if you have moderate or severe liver disease, as it can build up to dangerous levels in your body. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Talk to your doctor before taking ranolazine if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, as safety has not been fully established.
